$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the Sub-sessions settings: agent sessions that start their own sub-sessions (acpmux cmux-subsessions tools). The acpmux daemon embeds this file (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/hub/subsessions.rs) and takes the defaults and ranges from it; gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants. Row fields: see schemas/settings/source/updates.json.

lists.name: subsessions
lists.note: Settings > Agents > Sub-sessions: whether agent sessions may start sub-sessions, and how many and how deep. The daemon reads the file at each start, so a change applies at once.

rows.name: subsessionsEnabled
rows.note: Off: no session gets the cmux-subsessions tools, and a start is refused (subsessions.disabled).

help.text: An agent can start other agent sessions to work on parts of a task in parallel. They show under its session in the sidebar.

rows.name: subsessionsAnswerQuestions
rows.note: On: a session answers the questions (Claude Code AskUserQuestion, Grok and Cursor asks) of the sub-sessions under it (_acpmux/subsession/answer), never their permission prompts or plans. Off (the default, since it loosens the person-only answer rule): only the person answers them (subsessions.answers_off).

title.text: Let Sessions Answer Their Sub-sessions' Questions

help.text: When an agent in a sub-session asks a question, the session that started it can answer, and the answer shows who gave it. Permission requests always wait for you. Off: only you answer.

rows.name: subsessionsMaxChildren
rows.note: Live sub-sessions (running, waiting for input, or with a harness process alive) one session may have at a time. Finished, dead and closed sub-sessions do not use a slot. A session or an ancestor can set a lower value for a subtree.

help.text: The most live sub-sessions one session can have at the same time. Running, waiting and harness-alive children count; finished, dead and closed children do not use a slot.

rows.name: subsessionsMaxRunning
rows.note: Sub-sessions of one session that run a turn at the same time. More wait queued and start as running ones finish; lowering it stops none. A chat's own value (_acpmux/subsession/limits {sessionId}) and its workspace's ({workspaceId}) come before this one.

help.text: The most sub-sessions one session runs at the same time. More wait their turn and start as running ones finish. Running ones are never stopped when you lower it.

rows.name: subsessionsMaxDepth
rows.note: The deepest level of nesting: a top-level session is 0, its sub-sessions 1.

help.text: How many levels of sub-sessions can start under a session. 1 lets a session start sub-sessions that cannot start their own.
